Get started with L0glm

Source: vignettes/L0glm.Rmd
L0glm.Rmd

L0glm fits sparse generalized linear models using adaptive ridge and IRLS. The same interface covers ordinary GLMs, negative binomial counts, joint multinomial classification and Cox survival models. Coefficients are returned on the original predictor scale in a sparse matrix.

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tomwenseleers/L0glm", subdir="L0glm")

The source package lives in the repository’s L0glm/ directory. Windows source installation requires Rtools. Special families use mgcv; Cox responses use survival.

Fit a sparse model

Here two predictors carry the signal among thirty candidates.

set.seed(7)
X <- matrix(rnorm(400 * 30), 400, 30)
beta <- numeric(30)
beta[c(1, 8)] <- c(2, -1.5)
y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta) + rnorm(400)

fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE)
fit
#> L0glm fit
#> Family: gaussian   Link: identity 
#> Observations: 400   Selectable predictors: 30   Channels: 1
#> Selected rows: 2   Nonzero selectable coefficients: 2   Mandatory rows: 0
#> Lambda: 6.09 
#> Convergence (last pass per stage/channel):
#>      stage channels converged not_converged unavailable max_iterations
#>  selection        1         1             0           0             14
#>    relaxed        1         1             0           0              2

lambda="gic" sets a penalty of log(p) * log(log(n)) on the minus-twice-log-likelihood scale. relaxed=TRUE refits the selected support with negligible ridge penalization, giving the selected effects little shrinkage.

L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]
#>    gic TP FP FN TN F1_score MCC
#> 1 1160  2  0  0 28        1   1

True coefficients are supplied only to calculate recovery metrics; fitting uses X and y.

Predict and inspect 

predict(fit, X[1:5, , drop=FALSE])
#>        [,1]
#> [1,]  4.514
#> [2,] -1.922
#> [3,] -0.775
#> [4,]  1.140
#> [5,]  2.127
head(as.matrix(coef(fit)), 10)
#>        [,1]
#>  [1,]  2.04
#>  [2,]  0.00
#>  [3,]  0.00
#>  [4,]  0.00
#>  [5,]  0.00
#>  [6,]  0.00
#>  [7,]  0.00
#>  [8,] -1.42
#>  [9,]  0.00
#> [10,]  0.00
c(logLik=as.numeric(logLik(fit)), AIC=AIC(fit), BIC=BIC(fit), GIC=GIC(fit))
#> logLik    AIC    BIC    GIC 
#>   -571   1148   1160   1160

summary(fit) adds a compact coefficient display and convergence diagnostics. fitted(fit) returns fitted means for the training observations. For new data, predict() applies the model in the original predictor coordinates.

Change the family 

set.seed(8)
y_binary <- rbinom(400, 1, plogis(.3 + X[, 1] - X[, 8]))
binary <- L0glm.fit(X, y_binary, family=binomial(),
  lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100)
predict(binary, X[1:5, ], type="response")
#>       [,1]
#> [1,] 0.879
#> [2,] 0.440
#> [3,] 0.645
#> [4,] 0.863
#> [5,] 0.799

Standard family objects and links work as in stats::glm(). Add an intercept with intercept=TRUE; binomial and multinomial fits include one by default. See the negative binomial, multinomial and Cox tutorials for their response formats.

Choose a workflow

Task Main function
One fast preset fit L0glm.fit(..., lambda="gic")
Tune a penalty using an information criterion L0glm.tune(..., tune="gic")
Cross-validate prediction deviance L0glm.tune(..., tune="cv", nfolds=5)
Compare sparse regression methods sparseglm()
Score predictions and support recovery L0glm.metrics()
Screen an ultrahigh-dimensional design L0glm.fit(..., screen="ISIS")

Continue with model selection, weights and validation stopping, or the million-predictor example.
